newsitem.title: INDIA: India committed to economic reforms - president.
newsitem.headline: India committed to economic reforms - president.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma said on Thursday that the government is committed to economic reforms aimed at spurring economic growth.

In a prepared speech to parliament at the start of its budget session, Sharma said the centre-left government's goal of ensuring annual growth of gross domestic product of at least seven percent over the next five years was feasible.
"The government is committed to economic reforms aimed at faster economic growth," Sharma said in his speech, which had earlier been cleared by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet.

"The Indian economy is firmly set on a high-growth path and our objective of ensuring at least seven percent growth during the Ninth Plan period is feasible," he said. The five-year Ninth Plan starts on April 1.

Sharma said the government remains committed to attracting at least $10 billion a year in foreign direct investment, and was "taking steps to attract long-term pension and insurance funds from abroad". He did not elaborate.

The president said the deficit on the nation's oil pool account -- money owed to Indian oil firms for selling petroleum products below world prices -- will reach 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) by March 31. "Healthy development of the oil sector in the country demands that the oil pool account is in balance," he said.
